name: VIPER22ASTR-E
title: Off-line primary switcher: 730 V power MOSFET with 60 kHz current-mode PWM
summary: VIPer22A-E puts a current-mode PWM controller and a 730 V power MOSFET on one die, for small mains-powered supplies such as charger adapters and standby or auxiliary rails. It switches at a fixed 60 kHz, starts itself from the drain through a high-voltage current source, and accepts 9 V to 38 V on VDD. Feedback is a current into FB, which lowers the peak drain current; at light load it skips cycles. Undervoltage lockout has hysteresis, and the overvoltage, overcurrent and overtemperature protections restart automatically. It comes in SO-8 and DIP-8.
key_figures: 15 Ω typ, 17 Ω max at 0.4 A, 25 °C

circuits.title: Rectangular U-I output characteristics for battery charger
circuits.description: An isolated flyback charger that holds both a voltage limit and a current limit. Mains enters through fuse F1, capacitor C3 and common-mode choke T2, is rectified by bridge D4 and smoothed on C4. The T1 primary runs from the bulk rail to DRAIN, clamped by the R1, C2, D1 snubber. The auxiliary winding, phased to conduct while the switch is on, feeds VDD through D3 onto C5. On the secondary, D2 in the return leg charges C1 at DCOUT; D5, from the same winding end in the opposite phase, charges C10 to supply the TSM101 and the optocoupler LED. R10 in the return line senses output current. The TSM101 holds two amplifiers and a reference: one compares the R6/R9 output divider with the reference, the other compares the R10 drop (offset by R5/R7 from the reference) against ground through R8. Their outputs are diode-ORed and either one pulls current through the optocoupler LED via R2. The phototransistor feeds current from VDD into FB, filtered by C6. R3/C8 and R4/C9 compensate the two loops. Because the controller supply is taken in forward mode, current regulation keeps working with the output near 0 V.

circuits.title: Rise and fall time test circuit
circuits.description: Drain switching times are taken on a clamped inductive load: inductor L from a 300 V supply to DRAIN, with clamp diode D and a small capacitor C (much less than Coss) across it. tf and tr are read on VDS between its 10 % and 90 % points.

circuits.title: Restart duty-cycle test circuit
circuits.description: FB is held at 2 V and DRAIN sits at 100 V. The start-up source charges the VDD capacitor from VDDoff to VDDon (time tCH); switching then stays off and the part's own supply current discharges the capacitor back to VDDoff (time tST), and the cycle repeats. DRST is tST over the whole period.
notes: 10 F is a misprint for 10 µF.

circuits.title: Peak drain current vs feedback current test circuit
circuits.description: VDD is fed from 18 V and a current source drives IFB into FB, which carries 47 nF to SOURCE. DRAIN switches a 4 mH inductor from a 100 V supply; a 100 V zener in series with a diode clamps the inductor. The peak drain current is read against IFB, giving GID, IDlim, IFBsd and RFB.

operation.text: Fixed 60 kHz switching, current-mode control, VDD from 9 V to 38 V, undervoltage lockout with hysteresis on the auxiliary supply, a high-voltage start-up source fed from DRAIN, and overtemperature, overcurrent and overvoltage protection with automatic restart. Light load brings automatic burst mode; overvoltage is handled in hiccup mode. Uses named: charger adapters, standby supplies for TVs and monitors, auxiliary supplies for motor control.

VDD works from 9 V to 38 V. Fed in forward mode from the auxiliary winding, the part gets energy as soon as it starts switching, so the VDD capacitor can shrink to a 100 nF ceramic chip and start-up time from mains switch-on to output is much shorter. With the secondary controller also fed in forward mode, current regulation holds even with the output at or near 0 V. In forward mode VDD follows the input voltage, varying about 4 to 1 over a wide-range mains input.

FB takes a current, not a voltage. Inside, the MOSFET's sense current IS (proportional to ID) and the FB current both flow into a 230 Ω resistor R2, whose voltage a comparator checks against about 0.23 V; FB reaches the sense node through a 1 kΩ resistor R1. More FB current means a lower peak drain current. The 60 kHz oscillator sets the PWM latch and the comparator resets it.

IDlim as computed assumes FB at 0 V, which an optocoupler pulling FB up never quite allows, so an application stops a little short of it. The capacitor on FB averages the pin voltage; at start-up or under a short circuit, with the optocoupler off, FB is close to 0 V.
If IFB exceeds IFBsd the part stops switching. Before that, once the drain current falls to about 12 % of IDlim (85 mA), the part skips cycles in burst mode, which matters at light load.

Blanking makes a minimum on time, so there is a lowest peak drain current, tONmin × VIN / L, under which the current is not controlled linearly. It is set by primary inductance and input voltage; whether it lies above or below the 85 mA burst threshold gives two different shapes of the ID against IFB transfer function.

Once input voltage is applied, the start-up source charges the VDD capacitor from DRAIN for as long as VDD is below VDDon. At VDDon the source turns off and switching begins at full current, since no optocoupler current reaches FB yet. The output rises to its regulation point, the secondary loop starts driving the optocoupler, and FB then carries the current that matches the load. Over the start phase tss the VDD capacitor alone powers the part until the auxiliary winding supplies it; a capacitor too small lets VDD reach VDDoff first and the converter does not start.
When VDD exceeds VDDovp the part resets itself and stops switching. The stop is latched only until VDD has fallen to VDDoff; then normal operation resumes on its own.

At TSD (170 °C typ) switching stops and the start-up source delivers no current, so VDD collapses. When the junction has cooled by THYST (40 °C typ) the start-up source recharges VDD and the part restarts by itself at VDDon.

With FB held at 2 V and DRAIN at 100 V, VDD ramps from VDDoff up to VDDon on the start-up current (tCH), then falls back to VDDoff on the part's own supply current (tST), and so on. DRST = tST / (tST + tCH), 16 % typ.

A TSM101 (two op amps and a voltage reference, outputs diode-ORed) drives the optocoupler and regulates output voltage and output current together, giving a voltage limit and a current limit. Chargers that run mostly at a set charge current use this, and Li-ion cells need both modes.
RthJA is quoted on single-sided FR4 with 200 mm² of copper, at least 35 µm thick, joined to all DRAIN pins.
